newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down, but off lows; mild recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down, but off lows; mild recovery seen.

text.p: The ringgit is expected to stage a mild recovery next week as fresh overseas funds arrive to take advantage of an expected rise in Malaysian interest rates, dealers said on Friday.
It ended lower in Kuala Lumpur on Friday, but was off the day's lows on profit-taking in dollar/ringgit by overseas funds.
"There was a big chunk of dollars sold, said to be by a U.S. bank out of Germany. Nearly 100 (million) dollars was sold,' said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5073/83 per dollar against 2.5070/77 on Thursday. It hit a low of 2.5110 in the morning.
The Malaysian bank dealer said overnight dollar buying against ringgit by funds and corporate dollar demand during Asian time from Kuala Lumpur caused the ringgit's fall.
"But yield differential should bring some of the funds back," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said payment for a two billion ringgit, seven-year government bond issue on Monday would reduce liquidity in the domestic money market and pull up interest rates.
Dealers said the ringgit would trade in a 2.5050/5150 range for the next few days.
